title: Skald configuration
description: The skald: section of application.yml, generated from spec/configuration-v1.json. Other sections (proxy:, spring:) are left open.

endpoint.description: The S3-compatible object store (MinIO, Ceph, AWS S3) holding bundles and build logs. Unset: the publishing layer's storage is off and the application boots as upstream.

region.description: The store's region; most self-hosted stores accept any value.

access-key.description: SECRET: give it as ${VARIABLE} or through configtree:, never in the file. The store's access key id. Required with endpoint.

secret-key.description: SECRET: give it as ${VARIABLE} or through configtree:, never in the file. The store's secret key. Required with endpoint.

path-style.description: Path-style bucket addressing. On by default, unlike the SDK: a self-hosted store behind one hostname has no wildcard DNS. Turn off for AWS S3.

require-override.description: Refuse to start when the dispatcher override that runtime-added content needs could not be installed. false starts anyway, and content published at run time will not open.

max-running.description: App builds running at once across the whole deployment, counted in the database.

queue-capacity.description: Builds that may wait (QUEUED) across every content item. May be raised, never removed.

per-publisher-active.description: Queued, running and publishing builds one publisher may hold at once.

lease.description: How long a build's claim lasts without renewal before the reaper interrupts it. Long enough to outlast a stalled host: a holder survives a stall of lease minus renew-every.

renew-every.description: How often a running build renews its claim; at most half the lease.

deadline.description: A build's wall-clock deadline; past it the build is TIMED_OUT.

enabled.description: Shared Linux binaries for R packages: compile each package once in a sandbox and serve it from forge. Off by default. The shared-binaries path has not had Skald's own security review yet: until a release says it has, enable it only on a deployment that accepts that a binary's integrity rests on forge and the uploader. Needs the worker and forge-url.

max-running.description: Package compiles running at once, beside the app builds.

max-attempts.description: Claims per package before it is FAILED and its apps keep restoring it from source.

lease.description: How long a compile's claim lasts without renewal.

renew-every.description: How often a compile renews its claim; at most half the lease.

deadline.description: One compile's wall-clock deadline. Large packages (duckdb) compile for well over an hour on a busy host.

forge-url.description: forge's base URL, ending in /. Unset: shared binaries are off. No credentials, query or fragment in it.

forge-token.description: SECRET: give it as ${VARIABLE} or through configtree:, never in the file. forge's write token, scoped to bin/linux/<codename>-<arch>/contrib/<rminor>/** of the binary repository. Required with forge-url. Never handed to any container.

forge-registration-ttl.description: How long forge's platform registration is trusted before it is read again.

forge-timeout.description: Connecting to forge and each small exchange.

forge-upload-deadline.description: One binary's upload, which grows with the binary.

source-repository.description: forge's CRAN proxy member (never the group, which also serves hosted packages), ending in /, from which sources are verified against the public index. Unset: nothing is verified.

source-max-expanded-size.description: A source tarball's largest expanded size.

source-index-ttl.description: How long a fetched index is reused.

source-behind-retry.description: When the index is behind the lock, the first retry; it doubles from there.

source-behind-max-retry.description: The longest wait between retries of an index behind the lock.

source-behind-bound.description: How long after the first try a package whose index stays behind is refused INDEX_BEHIND; forge caches a proxy's index for 24 hours by default.

source-archived.description: Also build archived versions the index no longer lists, trusting their first fetch (its SHA-256 is recorded and never changes).

enabled.description: Run builds on this instance's Docker host. Needs a database, object storage and every key the worker marks required.

owner.description: This instance's name on the builds it claims. Unset: the host name.

worker-image.description: The build worker image (images/buildkit-worker), by digest.

gateway-image.description: The egress gateway image (images/egress-gateway), by digest.

registry.description: The registry's host name as the worker reaches it (port 5000); built images and the published bases live there.

registry-api.description: The registry as this instance reaches it, http(s)://host[:port], for publication's digest check. The credential travels in a Basic header: prefer https or an address on this host.

registry-username.description: The registry user builds push as.

registry-password.description: SECRET: give it as ${VARIABLE} or through configtree:, never in the file. That user's password.

outer-networks.description: Docker networks the gateway joins to reach the registry and the mirrors.

repos.description: Hosts of the package repositories the gateway lets a build reach.

private-mirrors.description: Hosts of private package mirrors the gateway lets a build reach.

cran-mirror.description: The CRAN mirror R builds restore from (forge's CRAN group); its host must be in repos or private-mirrors.

pypi-mirror.description: The PyPI simple index Python builds install from; its host must be in repos or private-mirrors.

cran-linux-binaries.description: The CRAN mirror has forge's Linux binary layout (<cran-mirror>__linux__/<codename>/latest). Off by default: a mirror without it answers 404 and renv does not fall back to source.

published-bases.description: The published-bases file dev/publish-bases.py wrote: each base's digest in the registry.

workspace.description: A writable directory this instance alone extracts bundles into; locked at startup.

architecture.description: The architecture this host builds for.

quota.description: Each build's workspace quota. At least 1GB; a cold R build holds the extracted base, BuildKit's snapshots and the compiled library.

poll.description: How often a running build's stop and log are checked; at most half the coordinator's renew-every.

settle.description: How long a stopped build is given to wind down before its worker is removed.

idle-pause.description: The build loop's pause when the queue is empty.

sweep-period.description: How often the reconciliation sweep removes what no live attempt owns.

sweep-grace.description: How long after a build ends the sweep leaves its attempt alone; longer than settle and the disposal's close wait.

pool-size.description: Ready workers per published base, warmed ahead of any build. 0: every build launches its own. Each idle one holds a worker, a gateway, a loop device and a workspace image.

parallel.description: Builds this instance's Docker host runs at once. At most skald.builds.max-running, the limit for the whole deployment, which every instance's builds count against.

pool-ttl.description: How long a ready worker is kept before a fresh one replaces it.

bundle-bucket.description: The object store bucket holding bundles.

log-bucket.description: The object store bucket holding build logs.

max-compressed-bytes.description: The uploaded archive as it arrived. Checked against the byte count before a single header is parsed, so it is the first bound anything hits. (unit: bytes)

max-expanded-bytes.description: Total bytes written across all members. Counted from bytes actually streamed, not from declared sizes, so a lying header cannot buy room. (unit: bytes)

max-entries.description: Physical headers, including directories, extended headers and anything else parsed and ignored. Metadata counts: an archive of nothing but ignored headers is still an archive the parser walked. (unit: count)

max-manifest-bytes.description: The manifest member. Distinct from max_file_bytes and always the smaller of the two in practice, because the manifest is parsed into memory as a document rather than streamed to disk. (unit: bytes)

max-extended-header-bytes.description: One PAX extended header's own payload. tarfile never reports this, which is why the corpus fixture bomb-huge-pax-field is accepted by a library-only extractor. (unit: bytes)

max-path-bytes.description: The member path in UTF-8, after any approved PAX override, excluding the extraction root. (unit: bytes)

max-segment-bytes.description: One path segment in UTF-8. (unit: bytes)

max-depth.description: Path segments in a member, counted after validation. (unit: count)

extraction-deadline-seconds.description: Wall clock for one extraction, enforced by the extractor itself. The corpus oracle applies its own outer deadline on top, because a bound a subject enforces on itself is a bound that has to be checked from outside. (unit: seconds)
